short: Outstanding balances grouped by how long they have been due.
seoTitle: Aging Report — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: An aging report groups outstanding invoices into buckets by how long they have been overdue — current, 1–30 days, 31–60, 61–90 and beyond.
definition: An aging report groups outstanding invoices into buckets by how long they have been overdue — current, 1–30 days, 31–60, 61–90 and beyond. It exists for both receivables and payables.
bodyHtml:
Why Aging Report matters

A single total tells you how much is outstanding; the ageing tells you how worried to be. Recovery odds fall sharply with each bucket, which is why age matters more than amount.

Aging Report formula

Days overdue = Today − Invoice due date

Bucket every open invoice by that figure.

How Aging Report works in practice

Chase by bucket, starting with balances just past due where recovery is easiest. On the payables side, use the same report to pay to terms rather than to pressure.

faq.question: How often should I run an aging report?
faq.answer: Weekly for receivables in a credit business, monthly at the very least.

faq.question: Which bucket should I focus on?
faq.answer: The 1–30 day bucket. Collection rates drop steeply once invoices pass ninety days.
